item.title: #3583135: An optional map property's default value never reaches the tool
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +535/−22 · php +522/−19 · md +13/−3
  • Diff: 6ba8be7
  • Discussion: #3583135 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

When a caller sends a map input but leaves out an optional property that declares a default_value, the tool now receives that default. Previously the input schema advertised the default (for example "size": "medium"), but the tool saw an empty map. The same now holds for nested maps, maps inside lists, and maps keyed by name. Falsy defaults such as FALSE, 0 and '' are now advertised in the schema too.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

TypedInputsTrait::getExecutableValue() is restructured so every value source (locked, input, configuration, default) passes through a new private withPropertyDefaults() before prepareExecutableValue() and validation. The method walks MapDataDefinition properties, ListDataDefinition items, and the item values of a MapInputDefinition that has an item definition. It fills a property only if it is absent, optional, and has a non-NULL default, and it recurses into the filled default.

Required properties are not filled, so a missing required property is still reported by validation. An absent optional map still stays NULL, and a property sent as null stays null. The issue says that case waits on #3583106.

In InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer, the schema default check changes from truthiness to !== NULL, so FALSE, 0 and '' defaults are advertised. To stop a multiple definition's empty-list default from now appearing on each item, the cloned item definition gets setDefaultValue(NULL). This also removes the earlier documented difference where a default value was no longer advertised on each item. SchemaSampleGeneratorTrait now builds a sample for a keyed map from its additionalProperties item schema. The diff adds the map_property_default_tool test tool, and a kernel test, MapPropertyDefaultTest, covers it.

item.title: #3586867: Raise the contrast of muted and tinted text in the AI API Explorers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +60/−18 · css +60/−18
  • Diff: f9b7a17
  • Discussion: #3586867 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

Text in the AI API Explorers is easier to read. In Gin dark mode the muted text (run chips, segmented controls, view switches, task descriptions) was 4.21:1 against its background, below the 4.5:1 WCAG 2.2 asks for. It is now lighter. Status pills, hub filter counts, the Embeddings similarity matrix, and the faded rows in Rerank and the threshold bars were also changed so their text reaches the required contrast in light and dark mode.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: AI API Explorer CSS tokens changed: --aie-muted is lighter in Gin dark, --aie-primary-text is now a mix, and new --aie-danger-text and --aie-green-text tokens exist; custom themes overriding these may need review.

Technical details

The main fix is in css/explorer-ui.css. Inside .gin--dark-mode .aie, --aie-muted is now color-mix(in srgb, var(--gin-color-text-light, #545560) 75%, var(--aie-text)). It is built from Gin's token rather than from itself, which would loop. --aie-muted-strong is mixed from it, so it gets lighter too. Gin light is not touched.

Coloured text now uses new tokens mixed towards --aie-title: --aie-primary-text (65% of the Gin primary), --aie-danger-text, --aie-green-text, and a stronger --aie-warning-text (45% instead of 60%). They are used by .aie-status--ok and .aie-status--error, .aie-tools__req, .aie-tools__arg and .aie-rerank__row--up .aie-rerank__move. The pressed .aie-hub__filter .aie-count swaps its colours (primary text on an --aie-on-primary background). .aie-btn--primary:active is listed so Gin's a:active colour does not override the button text. Selected file, task and size cards switch their secondary text to --aie-muted-strong on the tinted selection.

Faded rows no longer use opacity on text. .aie-bar--dim and .aie-rerank__row--below now fade only the bar fill (.aie-bar__fill, .aie-rerank__fill), and the label, text and value keep --aie-muted. In embeddings.css the matrix heat is capped at 35% of the accent (calc(var(--aie-heat, 6%) * 0.35)), so the title colour stays readable. .aie-embeddings__hi no longer switches to --aie-on-primary and is only bolder, and the legend gradient was adjusted to match.

item.title: #3586876: Chat Explorer fails with "Drupal is not defined" because its library declares no dependencies
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +5/−0 · yml +5
  • Diff: 158e68d
  • Discussion: #3586876 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The Chat Explorer in AI API Explorer no longer fails with "Drupal is not defined" on Drupal 12. Its JavaScript library did not declare its dependencies, so the browser could load the script before Drupal's core JavaScript and the explorer's behaviors never attached. The Embeddings explorer had the same gap and is fixed too.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml, explorer.chat and explorer.embeddings now declare dependencies: - ai_api_explorer/explorer_ui, as the other explorer libraries already do. That library pulls in core/drupal, core/drupal.ajax and core/once, which js/explorers/chat.js uses (Drupal.behaviors, Drupal.t, Drupal.formatPlural, once). Per the issue, Drupal 11 happened to order the scripts correctly, while Drupal 12 put the chat aggregate ahead of core/drupal. The commit also adds core/drupal.announce to the dependencies of explorer.decision.

item.title: #3594897: Explain metrics and terms on the admin pages, with a link to the glossary
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 39 files, +1091/−93 · php +894/−77 · md +105/−9 · css +47 · js +33 · yml +10 · txt +2 · neon +0/−7
  • Diff: cece135
  • Discussion: #3594897 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval's admin pages now explain their own jargon. Terms such as Overall error, Average gap, TPR, TNR, n, Split, Config version, Gate, Unscored, Corrected pass rate, Trend, Taxonomy, EEE and OTLP get a small "?" button. Clicking, tapping or pressing Enter on it opens a short definition with a "Learn more" link to the matching glossary entry on the docs site. Escape or a second click closes it. The calibration, judges, results, compare, traces, failure mode and import pages also get a short help text with a link to the relevant user guide. The glossary gained entries for the terms that had none.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Labels and headers on AI Eval admin pages now include a .ai-eval-toggletip button and popover bubble, which can change exact-text selectors.
  • New API: New ai_eval_toggletip render element with Toggletip::term() and Toggletip::cell() helpers, the ai_eval/toggletip library and generated GlossaryTerms::all() definitions.

Technical details

The definitions come from one source, docs/user/glossary.md. scripts/glossary-to-php.php parses the first paragraph of each entry with GlossaryMarkdown::parse() and writes src/Help/GlossaryTerms.php, a generated class of TranslatableMarkup strings keyed by glossary anchor, so the definitions can be extracted for translation. After editing a first paragraph you must rerun the script. A unit test (GlossaryTermsTest) compares the generated class with the glossary. The README documents the workflow.

The UI is a new render element, #type => 'ai_eval_toggletip' (Drupal\ai_eval\Element\Toggletip), with #term (the glossary anchor) and #label. Two static helpers wrap it: Toggletip::term($term, $label) for any render array, and Toggletip::cell($term, $label) for a table header or body cell. It renders the label, a <button popovertarget> and a <span popover> bubble using the native popover attribute, with no Ajax. The new ai_eval/toggletip library (css/toggletip.css, js/toggletip.js, depending on core/drupal and core/once) is attached only when a known term renders. The JS only positions the bubble near its button on toggle. An unknown anchor logs a warning once and falls back to the plain escaped label.

Placements cover the calibration list and detail pages, the judges table and validation history/compare, results list, detail and compare, failure rate table, failure mode list, trace review verdict filter and the two import forms. Some explanatory prose on those pages was removed in favor of the popovers, for example the TPR/TNR hover title text and the overall-error sentence on the callers form. Because a label cell now also contains the button and the definition text, existing tests that matched exact cell text were changed to starts-with(...) XPaths or strip the toggletip nodes. A new HelpHooks class implements hook_help for these routes and links to the guide pages. The glossary and the failure rate and average score definitions were also reworded. GraderPluginManager now names the deprecated annotation class as a string, and a phpstan baseline entry for it was removed.

Upgrade

Only relevant if you render your own admin tables or tests against AI Eval pages. To add a definition to a label, use the glossary anchor:

use Drupal\ai_eval\Element\Toggletip;

$header[] = Toggletip::cell('overall-error', $this->t('Overall error'));

Tests that match the exact text of an AI Eval label or header may need starts-with(normalize-space(.), "..."), since the cell now also contains the "?" button and its definition.

  • Committed: November 16, 2026

item.title: #3586862: Lay out right-to-left text in AI API Explorer results in its own direction
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +555/−19 · php +477/−18 · css +57 · md +21/−1
  • Diff: 719624f
  • Discussion: #3586862 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

Right-to-left text (Arabic, Hebrew, Farsi, Urdu) in AI API Explorer results, such as run titles, quotes, outputs, chat bubbles and transcripts, was laid out left to right, so it started at the left edge and its punctuation landed next to the first word. These blocks now take their direction from the text, so right-to-left text is right-aligned with punctuation at its end. English and other left-to-right text looks as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ExplorerUi::isolate() and ExplorerUi::languageDirection() added for explorer plugins that show free text or mixed labels.

Technical details

css/explorer-ui.css gets one rule with unicode-bidi: plaintext and text-align: start for the shared classes (.aie-run__title, .aie-quote, .aie-output) and for the explorer-specific blocks that hold free text (chat, extractive QA, rerank, speech to text, speech to speech, moderation, tools, object detection labels and others). plaintext takes each paragraph's direction from its first strong character. A second rule, .aie [dir] { unicode-bidi: isolate; }, keeps an explicit dir working, because plaintext would ignore it.

Two helpers are added to ExplorerUi. languageDirection(string $code) returns rtl or ltr from LanguageManager::getStandardLanguageList(), or NULL for an unknown code. isolate(string $text) wraps text in U+2068 and U+2069, which works like <bdi> but is also usable in attributes and <option> labels. The Translate explorer uses languageDirection() to set dir on the output from the target language and on the quote when the source language was picked, not detected, which fixes an Arabic translation that starts with a Latin word. Speech to Speech sets dir and lang on its texts. Embeddings labels ("T2 · text") use isolate(). The Speech to Speech and Text Classification run titles wrap file names and labels in <bdi>, and ObjectDetectionGenerator gives the label cell the aie-object-detection__label class. The module README gains a "Showing text in any language" section, and new Functional and FunctionalJavascript tests cover the behavior.

Upgrade

For custom explorer plugins that show user or model text: put the text in a block with aie-run__title, aie-quote or aie-output, or add your own class to the rule in css/explorer-ui.css. Where the language is known, set dir from ExplorerUi::languageDirection(). For a label that puts a prefix before a text, use <bdi> or ExplorerUi::isolate():

'label' => $label . ' · ' . ExplorerUi::isolate($names[$j]),

  • Committed: November 16, 2026 (3 days later)

item.title: #3586830: Add an Image-to-Video API Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +1353/−1 · php +1066/−1 · css +160 · js +118 · yml +9
  • Diff: 262b86f
  • Discussion: #3586830 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer now has an Image to Video Explorer at /admin/config/ai/explorers/image_to_video_generator. You upload an image, optionally describe the motion in a prompt, pick a provider and model, and get a playable video with a download button and a code example. It appears in the explorer list when an image_to_video provider is configured. Image-only models still work without a prompt, and provider errors are shown in the results area.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The explorer is a new plugin, ImageToVideoGenerator (#[AiApiExplorer], id image_to_video_generator, operation type image_to_video), registered in the av group of ExplorerHub. It follows the shared explorer UX of the other explorers: the ai_api_explorer_file input element for the image, the shared provider config element (providerElement('image_to_video', ...)), run history with "edit and run again" and "use as source" handling, and a generated code example via CodeExample.

On submit it builds an ImageToVideoInput from the image, calls setPrompt() only when a prompt was entered, and calls imageToVideo() on the provider. Every VideoFile in the normalized output is saved as a file via the run manager, so providers that return several videos are all shown. The video is rendered as a plain <video> element sized from the source image, since there is no shared video component. A new explorer.image_to_video library adds css/explorers/image_to_video.css and js/explorers/image_to_video.js. The JS shows the video shape and length once metadata loads, updates the "Output" shape line from the picked image, and pauses other videos when one plays. The diff adds a test class for the explorer.

item.title: #3586403: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Chat Generation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +6543/−1477 · php +3875/−778 · css +1570/−503 · js +1032/−139 · md +34/−44 · twig +26 · yml +6/−13
  • Diff: 15068d5
  • Discussion: #3586403 · 1 contributor · 30 comments

Summary

The Chat Explorer has been redesigned on the shared explorer layout. It now supports a full message history instead of a single message, with system, user, assistant and tool roles. Several chats can be kept and reopened when run history is on. Tool calls and their results are shown in the thread, and the model can be set to only show a call, run it, or run it and continue for up to 5 rounds. Request settings (model, tools, output, code) sit in tabs, chats can be imported and exported as JSON, and structured output answers are checked against the schema. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration element. The generated code example no longer contains the broken calls and unescaped values it had before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers, front-end developers and site owners.

  • Security: AiValidator no longer fetches external documents referenced by $ref in a user-supplied JSON schema; it returns a validation error instead.
  • Theme change: Chat Explorer renders through the new ai-api-explorer-chat.html.twig template; the ai_api_explorer/stream and ai_api_explorer/multiselect libraries are removed.
  • New API: ExplorerRunManager::getRuns() takes a new $sort argument (created or changed); new ai_api_explorer_chat theme hook and explorer.chat library.

Technical details

ChatGenerator was rewritten around a stored chat (an ExplorerRunInterface run) holding messages and settings (provider, tools, tool_mode, stream, structured, schema, guardrail_set). It is saved after every turn through ExplorerRunManager; with history off the chat lives in form state and the chats column only lists the open chat. Layout comes from a new ai_api_explorer_chat theme hook (template_preprocess_ai_api_explorer_chat() splits the form into chats, thread, settings and import), the explorer.chat library (css/explorers/chat.css, js/explorers/chat.js), and MAX_ROUNDS = 5 caps automatic tool rounds. Streaming is done in the new chat script, so the old stream.js, stream.css, multiselect.js and the multiple-select assets and their libraries are deleted.

ExplorerRunManager::getRuns() gains a $sort parameter (created default, or changed), and the purge of runs past the count limit now orders by changed, so a chat that is still used is kept over a newer but idle one.

The code example is built with \Drupal::service(...), passes the normalized tool definitions to new ToolsInput($functions), and escapes message text and schema values. Outside the explorer, AiValidator::validateSchema() now uses a UriRetriever backed by an empty PredefinedArray, so schema references inside the document resolve but a $ref to a URL or file is never fetched; it returns "The schema references an external document, which is not supported." The mdxeditor build also gets safeHtmlNodes so HTML in the markdown shows without scripts or event handlers (requires rebuilding the editor assets).

item.title: #3594896: Admin pages use several names for the same thing, such as target and test
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 117 files, +808/−745 · md +424/−363 · php +362/−360 · yml +22/−22
  • Diff: f8cf34c
  • Discussion: #3594896 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval admin pages, menus, Drush output and user docs now use one name for each concept. What was shown as an eval target is now a test, dataset examples and cases are questions, a saved fit or curve is a calibration, callers are decision automators, the model a test runs is the model under test, and the envelope import is EEE results. Route titles move to sentence case without the 'Eval' prefix (for example Results, Run detail, Compare runs, Prompt optimization). The Label traces tab is now Gold labeling, Compare two judges is Judge against judge, and Promote is shown as Add to dataset. The glossary notes the older names so people with old screenshots can still find them.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: None to config ids or schema; only user-facing labels changed (e.g. setting label 'Candidate runs per attempt' is now 'Runs per candidate', key optimizer_candidate_runs unchanged).

Technical details

This is a string-only change across 117 files: *.routing.yml, ai_eval.links.action.yml and ai_eval.links.task.yml titles, controllers, forms, src/Render/* fragments, entity labels, list builders and the ai_eval_decision_calibration submodule, plus Functional and Kernel tests and docs/user/** that quote the strings. Code identifiers, route names, entity and config ids (including the ai_eval_target entity type and /targets/ paths) and permission machine names are untouched, as the issue scoped them out. The /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/... paths are unchanged.

Drush output from src/Command/EvalRunCommand.php and the requirements messages in src/Hook/AiEvalRequirements.php now say Test "%s": instead of Target "%s":, and 'model under test' instead of 'evaluated model'. The status report entry 'AI Eval targets' is now 'AI Eval tests'. The settings label 'Candidate runs per attempt' became 'Runs per candidate'. docs/user/glossary.md gained entries for Question, Verdict, Conversation, EEE, Average gap and Failure mode taxonomy, and notes the older names (target, fit, Promote, Brier, Off by, envelope).

Upgrade

If you have scripts, CI log matchers or Behat/Functional tests that match the old text, update them. For example, Drush output now reads:

Test "%s": the quality gate used judges that have not passed validation: %s.

instead of Target "%s": ..., and the empty case reads No tests configured. Add tests in the admin UI or via config.. Link and button text such as 'Add eval target', 'Import envelope', 'Compare two judges' and 'Label traces' is now 'Add test', 'Import EEE results', 'Judge against judge' and 'Gold labeling'. Site translations of the old strings will need re-translating.

item.title: #3586856: Decision: report provider-side blocks as AiUnsafePromptException, and make automator rules abstain on a blocked request
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +360/−51 · php +325/−45 · md +35/−6
  • Diff: 12332dd
  • Discussion: #3586856 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

When a Decision automator request is blocked, either by a guardrail set or by the provider's own safety filter, the field now keeps its current values and the log gets a specific notice saying the request was blocked. Before, a block showed up as a generic "general error" warning that looked like a broken integration. Decision provider authors now have a documented way to report a whole-request block: throw AiUnsafePromptException.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: DecisionBoolean, DecisionChoice and DecisionScore generate() no longer throw AiUnsafePromptException (including AiDecisionBlockedException); they return no values and log a notice.
  • New API: DecisionAutomatorTrait::abstainWhenBlocked() (protected) runs a closure and returns [] when AiUnsafePromptException is thrown.

Technical details

The provider contract (decision_provider_contract.md) now says that a refusal is per question, while a block of the whole request must throw AiUnsafePromptException with the provider's reason code and message. The block should be checked before answers are built, so an empty answers is not reported as AiBrokenOutputException, and a block that arrives as an HTTP error is mapped the same way. AiDecisionBlockedException stays reserved for AI's own guardrails, since it needs a phase and results. No library code changed for this part; the ai_decision_test provider gained a BLOCK_MARKER that makes it throw, for tests.

In DecisionAutomatorTrait, the new protected abstainWhenBlocked(\Closure $generate, ...) catches only AiUnsafePromptException and returns []. The three rule bases wrap their whole generate() body in it (the body moved to a private generateValues()). The catch covers the whole body, not each request, so a block on any request of a multi-request rule, for example one request per item on a multi-value Boolean field, keeps the whole field. The notice names model, provider, entity type and id, field and the exception message. For AiDecisionBlockedException it also says whether the guardrails blocked before or after generation. Other errors such as AiBrokenOutputException still propagate, and runDecision() keeps its signature and still throws. The guardrail set description on DecisionRuleBase now mentions the notice. DecisionAutomatorExecutionTest was updated: the old post-block test now expects no exception, and new cases cover pre-generation blocks, provider blocks across all rules, and errors that are not swallowed.

Upgrade

Code that calls a Decision rule's generate() directly and catches AiUnsafePromptException should check for an empty result or the log instead. Custom rules built on DecisionAutomatorTrait can opt in:

return $this->abstainWhenBlocked(fn (): array => $this->generateValues($entity, $fieldDefinition, $automatorConfig), $entity, $fieldDefinition, $automatorConfig);

Decision providers whose API blocks a whole request should throw AiUnsafePromptException rather than return empty answers or refusals.

Contribution

item.description:

item.title: #3586692: Context items listing does not show its empty text or the "Add one" link
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +193/−4 · php +193/−4
  • Diff: b4126dc
  • Discussion: #3586692 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

The empty AI Context Items listing at /admin/config/ai/context/items now shows "There are no AI Context Items yet. Add one." with a working link to the add form. Before, it showed core's text without the link. The link appears only for users who can create context items, and it works on sites installed in a subdirectory.

Impact

item.title: #3586710: On AI agents, conditional subcontext uses the agent instructions as the task, not the user request
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +698/−13 · php +587/−9 · md +111/−4
  • Diff: 2977d83
  • Discussion: #3586710 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

For AI agents, automatic context selection now uses the user's request as the task, not the agent's system prompt. Conditional subcontext decisions now depend on the actual question. Before, they were made from the agent instructions, so the same result could be reused for every question. The provider set under "AI Provider/Model" in the CCC general settings now receives the first 500 characters of the user request instead of the agent instructions. That provider can differ from the agent provider, and the request may contain personal data. Sites that don't want this can turn off conditional subcontext AI decisions or use the same provider as their agents.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: The conditional subcontext decision provider now receives the first 500 characters of the user request on agents, which may contain personal data.
  • API change: On agents, AiContextSelection::getTask() returns the user request (or an empty string) instead of the agent system prompt; selection event subscribers must accept an empty task.

Technical details

AiContextBuildSystemPromptSubscriber::onBuildSystemPrompt() used to pass the system prompt to AiContextSelectionFactoryInterface::fromConsumer(). That prompt holds the agent instructions, default information tool output and the loop text, so getTask() returned it and the decision cache key changed on every loop. It now passes a stored user request, or '' when there is none, as on the generic chat path.

onAgentStarted() reads the request through the new readUserRequest(). It reads on loop 0, or when nothing is stored for the agent yet (a restored run starts above loop 0). The result is kept per agent ID in $userRequests, because BuildSystemPromptEvent has no runner ID. The first source with text wins: the latest user message of the agent chat input; the description of the agent task (TaskInterface::getDescription()); the latest user message of the event chat history. On a restored run (loop above 0) the history fallback is cut at the first tool call or tool result by getMessagesBeforeTools(), because the agent adds its own user messages after tool calls. Text is only trimmed, not stripped or shortened. A failure while reading is logged and leaves the task empty, and context is still injected.

Known limits from the issue: an agent that calls itself as a sub-agent shares one stored request. Code that dispatches BuildSystemPromptEvent without AgentStartedExecutionEvent gets the last stored request for that agent ID, or an empty task. Docs (events.md, index.md, subcontext.md, rag.md, api-stability.md) were updated. rag.md now shows an example that returns early on an empty task.

Upgrade

Subscribers of ai_context.selection.items_selected and ai_context.selection.text_rendered that use the task as a query must handle an empty string, as in the updated rag.md example:

$query = $event->getSelection()->getTask();
if ($query === '') {
  return;
}

item.title: #3601421: Docker group restart fails on Ubuntu 26.04: no sg or newgrp
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +121/−17 · bats +67/−2 · sh +54/−15
  • Diff: 14adf9c
  • Discussion: #3601421 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The One Line Installer no longer dies on Ubuntu 26.04 after installing Docker Engine. That release ships neither sg nor newgrp, so the new docker group membership could not be activated, and the installer waited 60 seconds for a Docker daemon it could not reach before failing. It now restarts itself with sudo -u "$USER" -g docker when sg is missing, so the install carries on. If neither works, it stops immediately with log-out advice instead of waiting.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In linux_ensure_docker, a new _docker_group_activator helper prints sg if available, else sudo, else nothing. sg remains the first choice. _reexec_under_docker_group now takes sg or sudo as an argument. With no activator, the installer calls die right away, skipping the 60 s wait. The message no longer mentions newgrp.

The sudo path builds its command in _docker_group_sudo_argv, which fills the DOCKER_GROUP_SUDO_ARGV array. It runs sudo -u "$USER" -g docker env ... bash <installer> <original args>. The issue notes that sudo-rs (the sudo on Ubuntu 26.04) ignores -E and drops variables such as INSTALLER_URL, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and WAYLAND_DISPLAY. So every exported variable (compgen -e) is passed back through env VAR=value. OLI_DOCKER_GROUP_REEXEC is excluded from that list and set to 1 explicitly, so the re-exec guard still prevents looping. New bats tests cover sg present, sg missing with sudo, neither available, and the argv construction.

item.title: #3594892: Decision calibrations can turn a probability into exactly 0% or 100%: fit with Platt scaling instead
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 25 files, +625/−55 · php +553/−24 · md +57/−29 · yml +15/−2
  • Diff: e6d4109
  • Discussion: #3594892 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

New decision calibrations in AI Eval are fitted with Platt scaling, a smooth S-shaped curve, instead of an isotonic step curve. The old fit could turn a probability into exactly 0% or 100%, even from one or two reviewed answers, which makes a wrong answer very costly in log loss. The new curve keeps the model's order and never returns exactly 0% or 100%. Calibrations already saved keep working as isotonic curves. A fit is refused with a message when the reviews run against the model's order, and the held-out check still saves a fit that scores worse as inactive.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: ai_eval.calibration.* config schema gains method and parameters (a, b); existing config defaults to isotonic.
  • New API: DecisionCalibratorInterface::applyCurve(), a $method argument on fit(), CalibrationFitRefusedException, and getMethod()/getParameters() on EvalCalibration.

Technical details

DecisionCalibrator::fit() takes a new $method argument, defaulting to DecisionCalibration::METHOD_PLATT (METHOD_ISOTONIC is still accepted). The Platt fit is a logistic regression on the clamped log-odds of the raw probability, with Platt's smoothed targets and a ridge prior (LAMBDA = 1.0) pulling the slope toward 1 and the curve's height at the centre of the training log-odds toward the model's own curve. The prior is applied at the centre rather than at log-odds 0, because a small, correctly ordered, overconfident set otherwise came out flat or reversed. It uses damped Newton steps. The fit throws the new CalibrationFitRefusedException (a subclass of \InvalidArgumentException) if it does not converge or if the slope is not positive. RecordedFitForm and CalibrationFromReviewsForm show that message as is, instead of the generic 'reload the page' error.

Storage: DecisionCalibration gains method and parameters (a, b), and EvalCalibration gains matching properties, getMethod() and getParameters(), plus config schema entries. Config without method reads as isotonic, so no update path is needed. For Platt curves knots holds 13 samples at fixed probabilities (0.01 to 0.99), for display only. EvalCalibration::matches() returns FALSE for a Platt curve with missing, non-finite or non-positive-slope parameters, so callers stay uncalibrated.

Application goes through the new DecisionCalibratorInterface::applyCurve($method, $parameters, $knots, $probability), which CalibrationStore, CalibrationSubscriber and RecordedDecisionSource now use instead of apply(). Platt output is clamped to [1e-6, 1 - 1e-6]. The calibration page's 'How answers are corrected' table shows the Platt samples at fixed probabilities, with <0.01% and >99.99% at the ends. The calibration tutorial and CHANGELOG are updated.

Upgrade

Code that applies a stored curve should call applyCurve() instead of apply() on the knots alone:

$calibrated = $this->calibrator->applyCurve(
  $curve->getMethod(), $curve->getParameters(), $curve->getKnots(), $probability,
);

Implementations of DecisionCalibratorInterface must add applyCurve() and the $method argument on fit(). Existing isotonic calibrations need no migration; refit to get a Platt curve.

item.title: #3586841: Forward Port from `1.x` to `2.x`
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 336 files, +21418/−12228 · php +19292/−6092 · md +1901/−97 · txt +105/−98 · yml +82/−485 · json +38/−4641 · gitignore +0/−2 · nvmrc +0/−1 · css +0/−68 · svg +0/−11 · js +0/−725 · sh +0/−8

  • Discussion: #3586841 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

This forward-ports features that had landed in 1.x to 2.x. The main addition is a Decision operation type: calling code asks true/false (noul), choice, score and box questions about shared text or structured state, optionally with images, and gets back probabilities and confidence it can threshold on. A default Decision provider can be chosen in AI settings, and an installed provider has to implement it. Guardrails (RegEx, Input Length Limit, Moderation) can run on Decision requests, the API Explorer gains a Decision Explorer, and AI Automators gain boolean, list and numeric field rules backed by Decision. Provider selection forms can now filter models by required capabilities and show what the selected model supports.

The commit also contains documentation and tooling updates. Only 21 of the 336 changed files were visible in the diff I was given, so this summary covers what those files and their docs describe.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: ai.settings default operation providers schema gains a decision entry ('Default decision provider').
  • New API: New decision operation type (DecisionInterface, DecisionInput, DecisionResponse, Drupal\ai\OperationType\Decision\Value question/answer classes), DecisionGuardrailInterface, and optional validate{OperationName}Input() provider hooks.

Technical details

Decision calls go through decision(DecisionInput $input, $model_id, $tags) on a provider and return a normalized DecisionResponse with typed getters (getNoul(), getChoice(), getScore(), getBox()). Helpers are isLikely() for noul and isConfident() for choice, score and box. Question state must be plain arrays, JSON scalars and NULL; objects, resources, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Invalid or incomplete provider answers raise AiBrokenOutputException. Choice and score answers are validated for probability totals, winner and weighted score, with an optional AnswerPrecision for providers that round values for transport. Without it the documented tolerance is 0.02. Box answers expose toPixels(), which rounds outward.

Guardrails: services.yml registers GuardrailExecutionContext, OperationGuardrailHandlerRegistry (a service_collector for the ai.guardrail_operation_handler tag), ChatGuardrailHandler, DecisionGuardrailRunner and DecisionValidationEventSubscriber. Only plugins implementing DecisionGuardrailInterface and declaring supportsOperation('decision', $phase) run on Decision requests, returning PassResult or StopResult. Reaching a set's threshold throws AiDecisionBlockedException, which extends AiUnsafePromptException. Per the docs, global sets attach at priority 100, validation runs at 20 and the guardrail handler at 10. Token-based length limits and similar unsupported checks in a caller-attached set raise AiSetupFailureException; in global sets they are skipped with a warning.

Operation types gain an optional input validator: ProviderProxy calls validate{OperationName}Input(Input $input, string $model_id): void on the configured provider before PreGenerateResponseEvent, so guardrails never see rejected input. The scaffolding skill docs and check script were updated to enforce the exact name and signature. ai_modules_installed() and a new ai_modules_uninstalled() now clear the ai_operation_types discovery cache.

The ai_provider_configuration element gets #capabilities, #show_capabilities and #capability_details_callback, and returns a use_default key. It lists only models declaring every required capability. A current selection that no longer qualifies stays visible, marked incompatible or unavailable. The selection is validated on submit. AiProviderPluginManager::getModelsWithCapabilities() applies the same rule outside forms.

public function validateChatInput(ChatInput $input, string $model_id): void {
  // Throw AiBadRequestException when the input cannot be handled.

item.title: #3594891: Decision calibrations for the judge are keyed on the model alias, not the model version that answered
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +1141/−81 · php +1091/−68 · md +46/−13 · yml +4
  • Diff: 3707238
  • Discussion: #3594891 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Decision calibrations are now tied to the model version the provider reports with each answer (for TypeSafe, jev-1.14.0), not the alias that was requested (jev-latest). Before, the judge and the field automator callers disagreed about what the model was, so a curve fitted on the Answer file tab with jev-latest never applied to automators. Now, when a provider moves an alias to a new version, the newest active curve for the same judge or automator and question keeps applying and is shown as carried over, until an active fit on the new version replaces it. Curves fitted for an alias before this release stop applying to the judge and need a new fit; automator curves fitted before this release are not carried over either.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_decision_calibration_update_10002() adds a requested_model column to ai_eval_decision_record.
  • Config change: ai_eval.calibration.* gains a requested_model string key.
  • New API: CalibrationApplierInterface::applyForAlias(), CalibrationStoreInterface::carried(), EvalCalibration::getRequestedModel(), and an optional $requestedModel argument on CalibrationStoreInterface::save().

Technical details

EvalCalibration gets a requested_model property (also in the ai_eval.calibration.* schema) holding the model id the caller asked for. ai_eval_decision_record gets a matching column, filled by DecisionRecorder from the event's model id, and RecordedDecisionSource::groups() passes the latest recorded value to RecordedFitForm, which stores it on the new fit. Update ai_eval_decision_calibration_update_10002() adds the column with an empty default, so rows recorded earlier have no requested model and their curves cannot carry over.

Lookup is now exact match first (CalibrationStore::fresh() on provider, reported model and fingerprint), then a new carried() method that returns the newest active curve for another model, filtered by a caller-supplied predicate. For automators, CalibrationSubscriber requires the curve's requested_model to be non-empty and equal to the event's model id, and the curve's scope to share a tag with the request, so switching the automator to another model stops the correction. A carried correction is marked with carried_from in the ai_eval_calibration metadata of the answer. For the judge, the new CalibrationApplier::applyForAlias() does the same with a predicate on the curve's requested_model or model_id equal to the judge's configured model.

The judge's served model is read from State (DecisionRubricGrader::SERVED_MODEL_STATE, a provider/requested/served mapping) via CalibrationJudgeUse::servedModel(), falling back to the configured model before the first grade. CalibrationJudgeUse::of() gains a CARRIED result and optional $state and $store arguments. The calibrations list, the calibration page and the Answer file and review fit forms use it for messages and for the default model, and add DecisionRubricGrader::SERVED_MODEL_CACHE_TAG to the cache metadata. RecordedDecisionSource::check() counts answers from another version when calibration_id is the curve, and the Callers tab reports how many. The shown diff does not include the DecisionRubricGrader changes themselves.

Upgrade

Run database updates so ai_eval_decision_calibration_update_10002() adds requested_model to ai_eval_decision_record. Then refit curves that were fitted for an alias such as jev-latest (they no longer apply to the judge), and refit automator curves fitted before this release, since they have no recorded requested model and are not carried over. On the Answer file tab, enter the model as the provider reports it, for example typesafeai__jev-1.14.0.

Code that implements CalibrationApplierInterface or CalibrationStoreInterface must add applyForAlias() and carried() respectively; CalibrationApplier now takes @ai_eval.decision_calibrator as a second constructor argument.
